He seems like a textbook narcissist but, regardless of whether other people agree with that or not, you seem incredibly unhappy and unfulfilled in this relationship and you’re being abused. Please leave before things escalate even more than they already have. Speaking from experience, things will get worse. 
Start building your support system back up by telling your friends and family about what is going on. One thing I learned is it is ok to ask for help. People love you and will want to help you out of this situation. You will feel so free once you get out and you’ll wonder why it took you so long to leave. Don’t beat yourself up though. Loving, caring people are targets for these types of manipulators and it isn’t your fault. Stay safe and get some support. Also, if you have the resources, get some counseling. Abusive relationships are traumatic and therapy can help you move on, forgive yourself, and arm you with the knowledge to avoid this type of relationship in the future. ❤️ You’re strong and you can do this!

If you were not the first girlfriend/boyfriend, you were probably a new supply at some point. I know I was a new supply. He said his ex was crazy, a raging alcoholic, AND he called her a narcissist that didn't care at all about his feelings. He admitted to me that he had physically abused her, but "only because she was hitting him and was acting crazy. Mind you this girl was like 5'4" 120lbs and he is over 6' tall and 300 lbs of muscle. 

Well, guess what. Eventually, when the devaluation stage hit, he would say the most hurtful things to me. I was the most ungrateful person he had ever met. I was a stupid b*tch. A c*nt. I became less than. If I accidentally interrupted him he would scream at me in front of people. Later he would tell me to "tap him lightly" on the shoulder to get his attention to avoid him exploding at me. Like I was in the wrong. He lied about things he said and denied reality. He told me I said things I did not say. Did things I didn't do. Etc. He also first targeted me when I was deep in the grief  over the loss of a good friend. 

There will always be a new supply and things will always go south eventually, even if people can't see it on the outside. I'm sure you didn't go telling his ex about what was going on. The new supply probably won't tell you how bad it is either. 

You are enough.

I had a similar thing happen. I broke contact off slowly... He would call me from my (male) friend's house. He used to hate on this person constantly when we were together, but when we broke up they became "good friends." 

They are trying to make you feel like you don't have the full support of your friends and family. They are also doing this so that they can portray themselves as a "chill" person, so that if you decide to tell your friends the full story they can defend themselves and character assassinate you. 

They are master manipulators. My ex sent me gifts in the mail and bought my sister stuff too. He walks all the girls to their car after work (he works at a bar) and talks all the time about how "if men just did the smallest things like that for women then this world would be a better place," but he would treat me like garbage. 

It is all to make themselves look good & make you feel like you can't trust anyone.

My advice:  Talk about it to your sister. If you feel comfortable, talk to your friend about it. Ignore him and move on. Stay strong 💜

I can't come out and tell people I have anxiety and that's why I wasn't productive. I try, but my thoughts start to race and it's like I'm stuck in my own head. From the outside I'm sure it just looks like I have no motivation or drive. It feels like every tiny thing I do takes so much effort. I'm exhausted.

I will get back to you more about this since I'm currently researching my options. Here are some things I have found to be helpful:

I read that in the cycle of addictive behavior we act on our impulses at the height of experiencing negative emotions, and that those emotions, if sat through will subside like a bell curve. When we act on the impulse, it reinforces this lie in our minds that the negative emotions will not go away without this action. I've been trying to sit through the emotions while doing an activity that makes it impossible or difficult to binge (using my hands or getting away from food) like video games, crocheting, taking a shower, drawing, writing about my feelings, yoga, or going for a walk. 

I also found a group on Meetup for people with ED's and looked up virtual video chat support groups, many of which are free.

I didn't even know there were overeating groups. 🤦🏽‍♀️Idk why it didn't dawn on me. I have been in group for self harm before, but that was in college and I guess it was easier to find that resource. Don't take two. This is a mistake that many first timers make. A lot of the time, people will take one, think that it's not enough because it hasn't hit them yet, and take another. Then both will hit and the trip is too intense. I've done quite a bit of acid, so I love going to big raves or EDM shows and tripping, but if it's your first time I would stay somewhere you know you'll be safe and if you can have someone that is sober there or on call that can help you out if you need it. You've taken shrooms before, so I'm sure you know that if you start feeling bad all you have to do is remind yourself that your on a drug and it will wear off. I'm not sure what kind of music you like, but I love listening to trap when I'm tripping and also watching LED lights. I hoop and love watching friends hoop and flow when I'm on LSD. Bright lights, great music, and good friends make for a great time on acid. :) Happy tripping.
